description: We are ASTRAVITA, a student team passionate about space exploration, technology, and innovation. Our name combines "Astra" (stars) and "Vita" (life), reflecting our vision of supporting human life among the stars. Our project is a health-monitoring platform for long-duration space missions. It tracks astronauts’ health, detects changes, provides explainable alerts, and guides crew members in using medical equipment and performing approved health checks when medical support is limited.
summary:
ASTRAVITA is an astronaut health monitoring and support platform designed for use during space missions. It brings together health monitoring, data analysis, practical guidance, and artificial intelligence in one system.

The platform allows users to monitor astronaut health readings, compare them with individual health baselines, track changes over time, and receive intelligent alerts when unusual patterns are detected. It also provides health reports and crew health comparisons.

Beyond monitoring, ASTRAVITA includes an educational section that guides users through medical procedures, explaining how to perform specific health checks and use monitoring equipment correctly.

Another key feature is its AI-powered assistant, designed to answer questions about crew members' health conditions, medical readings, and astronaut health-related procedures. It provides specialized information within its defined scope to help users better understand health-related situations.

Our goal is to make astronaut health information easier to monitor, understand, and manage throughout space missions.
details:
ASTRAVITA SpaceLab – Project Details

ASTRAVITA SpaceLab is a software platform designed to support astronaut health monitoring during space missions. It addresses the challenge of organizing, visualizing, and interpreting health-related information in an environment where continuous awareness of crew health is essential.

The platform provides an interactive dashboard where users can explore crew profiles, review simulated physiological health readings, observe trends, and access analytical insights. It brings health-related information together in one interface to make patterns easier to understand and support informed research and monitoring.

ASTRAVITA currently includes five fictional astronaut profiles created by our team for demonstration purposes. Its health readings are simulated data and are not real measurements from NASA astronauts or an operational space mission. The platform is designed as a research and demonstration prototype, not a medical diagnostic system.

The system was developed using React, TypeScript, and Vite for the frontend, FastAPI for the backend, and SQLite for data storage. Its design focuses on clear data visualization, structured information, accessibility, and the separation of simulated data from externally sourced reference information.

Our approach emphasizes transparency and responsible data interpretation. By combining crew profiles, health indicators, visual analytics, and an accessible interface, ASTRAVITA aims to demonstrate how software can help organize and communicate astronaut health information for future space exploration.

The project is a prototype that can be extended with validated physiological datasets, additional analytical capabilities, and future integrations.
